answer.rationale: The mandate requires 18% cost reduction and the incumbent refused renegotiation. memory_c2 demonstrates the low-cost vendor delivered sharp unit cost cuts with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing—this is the primary option. However, at 94% committed volume with no buffer, supply interruption risk is material. Switching to the low-cost vendor alone meets the cost mandate but eliminates negotiating room with the incumbent and increases concentration risk during the transition. memory_c4 shows renegotiation can unlock margin recovery, but the incumbent has already refused to reopen. The low-cost vendor quote meets the mandate standalone, making a switch viable. Verification of memory_c2 (prior success with this vendor) and memory_c4 (renegotiation effectiveness against incumbents) will confirm whether the low-cost vendor is reliable enough to shoulder primary supply at current volumes, and whether a negotiation path remains open. Standard experiment scale allows controlled onboarding while observing performance before full commitment.
